news.title: New claims against Infantino deepen a turbulent period for world football's governing body
news.lede: According to The Telegraph, the Italian-Swiss lawyer, who served as secretary general of European football's governing body from 2009 to 2016, also previously used his influence to secure a promotion for the same UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship. Infantino has categorically denied the allegations, according to the article, which was published on Saturday. When contacted by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency on Saturday, a FIFA spokesperson had not responded. According to The Telegraph, which did not cite its sources, this employee received a "six-figure sum" upon her departure — at an unspecified time — in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around £45,000 (AU$86,000).

news.title: ‘Will not tolerate’: FIFA dig heels in as feisty statement fires back at president’s enemies
news.lede: FIFA have condemned efforts to oust Gianni Infantino as the governing body’s president in a statement released in response to allegations of an affair with a colleague during Infantino’s time as UEFA’s secretary-general. A FIFA spokesperson told the Telegraph, who originally reported the details of the alleged affair, promotion to a managerial role, six-figure sum payout upon departure and payment for business school, that Infantino “strongly denies” the allegations and that they are “categorically untrue”. news.title: Morocco, Algeria reach WAFCON semis, book World Cup spots
news.lede: JOHANNESBURG: A triumphant night for north Africa ended Saturday with hosts Morocco and Algeria reaching the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) semifinals and securing places at next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil. They took contrasting paths to quarter-final success, with Morocco building a two-goal lead before defending resolutely against South Africa for a 2-1 victory in Rabat, while Algeria came from behind against Ivory Coast in Casablanca to win by the same scoreline. The four WAFCON semifinalists qualify automatically for the World Cup, which will be held from June 24 to July 25, 2027. For Algeria, the victory secured a historic first appearance at the women’s World Cup.

news.title: "There Was a Reason for 'Messi's Tears' at the World Cup": Father Jorge Passes Away at 68; "The Quiet Supporter Who Created the 'God of Football'"
news.lede: 'God of Football' Lionel Messi (39, Inter Miami)'s father and long-time supporter, Jorge Messi, has passed away at the age of 68. According to Argentine media outlets Clarin and Infobae on the 8th (local time), Jorge Messi died in a hospital in Rosario, Argentina, after battling a chronic illness for a long time. He was more than just a father; he was the person who raised Messi into the world's best soccer player. In 2000, at age 13 when Messi required growth hormone treatment, Jorge traveled directly to Spain to secure Messi's signing and support contract with FC Barcelona.

news.title: Mosimane takes charge of a World Cup national team
news.lede: South Africa's National Executive Committee has approved the return of Pitso Mosimane to lead the Bafana Bafana national team, following the departure of Hugo Broos. Africa Soccer reported that the committee settled the decision during an extraordinary meeting at the football association's headquarters. Mosimane won strong backing to return and succeed Broos, who announced his exit from the head coach role last month after leading Bafana Bafana to the round of 32 at the 2026 World Cup. South African Football Association president Danny Jordaan said a few final matters still needed sorting before the appointment becomes official.

news.title: Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller thinks MLS has gained prestige because of the World Cup
news.lede: In his personal monthly newspaper, Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller spoke about the upcoming MLS season and what he’s been focused on these last few weeks.
